# Parihānikathā (Kv 1.2)

**ID:** Kv 1.2  
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)  
**Collection:** Abhidhamma  
**Title (Pali):** Parihānikathā  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul1.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul1.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Parihānikathā* (Kv 1.2) is the second section of the first chapter (*vagga*) of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The controversy addresses the pivotal question of whether an arahant can undergo retrogression or fall away (*arahā parihāyati* / *arahattā parihāni*) [Skorupski 1991; Waldron 2003]. According to the commentarial tradition, non-Theravāda groups such as the Sammatīyas, Vajjiputtiyas, Sabbatthivādins, and certain Mahāsaṅghikas maintained that an arahant could experience decline due to an eruption of passion (*rāgaparyuṭṭhita*) conditioned by latent underlying dispositions (*anusaya*); Theravāda debaters reject this, denying that fully liberated beings retain such dispositions [Waldron 2003].
